Top stem candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight.

Now I'll view one reference per class across 4 candidates.
That Alternaria reference was a microscopic spore view. Let me view the other 3 classes now.

**Analysis:**

Test image: A stem with a very dark brown/black external canker lesion localized at a node, surrounding stem is green, with dead shriveled leaves attached.

Comparison:
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Reference was microscopic (spores), but description matches well — "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers on stems." The dark canker with dried leaves above is consistent.
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: Reference showed internal vascular/pith decay (cut stem cross-section), not an external dark canker. Doesn't match.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Shows bleached white mycelium and sclerotia at soil line. No white mycelium visible in test image. Doesn't match.
- **Southern_Blight**: Shows bleached internal tissue with dark border. Different morphology from the external dark canker in test image.

The test image best fits Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers: dark brown/black stem canker, localized at a node, with wilting/dying leaves above consistent with stem girdling.
